## Why This Is Asked

Tests the end-to-end path for feature flag gating and RBAC, ensuring frontend visibility aligns with backend flag state and permissions across services.

## Key Concepts

- Feature flags and RBAC integration
- Per-tenant/test data seeding and isolation
- End-to-end verification across API, frontend, and messaging backend
- Rollback and UI state reconciliation

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-endpoint to toggle flag (tenant-scoped)
async function enableFlag(tenantId, flag){
  await fetch(`/api/flags/${flag}?tenant=${tenantId}`, { method: 'POST' })
}

// Pseudo-test snippet (Playwright/Cypress-agnostic)
await enableFlag('tenant-123', 'instant_reactions')
// login as privileged user and navigate to channel
// assert emoji picker exists
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you ensure test isolation if multiple tests run in parallel on the same tenant?
- How would you simulate a partial failure (flag enabled, but feature backend failing) and verify fallback behavior?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests for offline-first flows are common in modern apps; this checks basic E2E coverage, data integrity, and sync behavior.

## Key Concepts
- Offline-first UI and service workers
- Background sync and idempotent requests
- Network emulation, data seeding, test isolation
- Conflict handling strategies for concurrent edits

## Code Example
```javascript
// Example Cypress-like flow (pseudo)
cy.visit('/notes')
cy.window().then(w => w.navigator.onLine = false)
cy.get('#new-note').type('Offline note')
cy.get('#save').click()
cy.window().then(w => w.navigator.onLine = true)
cy.wait('@backgroundSync')
cy.get('.note-item').should('contain', 'Offline note')
```
